title: GitHub Copilot coding agent ships inference-time self-evolving memory by Q2 2027
body: On June 29 the WorldEvolver arXiv paper (2606.30639) showed that letting a world model keep updating at inference time — via episodic memory, semantic rules distilled from prediction errors, and selective foresight that filters unreliable predictions — beats competing baselines on action-outcome accuracy and downstream task success while the core agent stays frozen, no fine-tuning required. That maps onto the dominant pain point in shipping coding-agent harnesses: agents take wrong actions because they mispredict consequences across long multi-step tasks. The structural force is cost: runtime memory and world-model adaptation is a far cheaper reliability lever than retraining a frontier backbone, and harness vendors are already converging on persistent agent memory (the AI Engineer World's Fair Harness Engineering keynote on July 2 signals exactly this focus). The forecast: a major coding-agent harness — most plausibly GitHub Copilot's autonomous coding agent — ships a runtime memory/world-model-adaptation feature that persists task-outcome learnings across a session or repository and carries a named task-success or reliability improvement, by Q2 2027.

reasoning.so_that: A major coding-agent harness ships a runtime memory/world-model feature with a named task-success or reliability gain
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; GitHub Copilot autonomous coding agent (or peer harness)
reasoning.plain_language: Coding-agent tools will soon learn from their own mistakes mid-task, without retraining the AI, to mess up less.

summary: A June 29 arXiv paper (WorldEvolver) showed a world model that evolves at inference time — using episodic and semantic memory plus selective foresight — improves agent action-prediction and task success without retraining the frozen backbone. Because runtime memory adaptation is cheaper than fine-tuning, a major coding-agent harness such as GitHub Copilot's autonomous agent is forecast to ship a runtime memory/world-model-adaptation feature with a named reliability gain by Q2 2027.
